task that is not parked; rejects for an unknown one.

symbols.name: TaskScheduler.blockedReason
symbols.comment:
Why a live task cannot run here, if it cannot: its definition (missing, too old, failed migration) or the restart
limit. A running task, an abort-marked one, and one holding its outcome are never blocked.

symbols.name: TaskScheduler.subscribeBlocked
symbols.comment: Call `listener` when blocked reasons may have changed without a commit: a registry change or a failed migration.

symbols.name: TaskScheduler.wake
symbols.comment:
When the Session next needs a process: `active` while some task can run now or is running, `at` for the earliest
sleep not yet due. Synchronous, from memory; a task whose chain is not loaded yet counts as it would alone.

symbols.name: TaskScheduler.join
symbols.comment:
Signal every invocation and wait for them, then write the tasks they ran back as `pending` (`writeAtClose`), as a
close is not a crash. Close calls this after every close listener has run, so waits, watches, and streams a task
holds end with the Session's reason, not as cancelled by its signal.

symbols.name: TaskScheduler.abort
symbols.signature: async abort(id: TaskId, context: Context, keepRestart = false): Promise<"marked" | "terminal">
symbols.comment:
Commit the abort mark, or settle a task that no registered definition can take as `orphaned` when nothing it owns
is live, then join the run invocation seen on the line; the commit listener signalled it. The abort invocation
starts once the task's ordinary owned work is gone. A `completing` task is only marked. A request replaces a
`restart` mark, so a task abandoned after a restart that waits for its definition is orphaned; with `keepRestart`,
as for an owner's own cleanup, such a task keeps its mark and waits on.

symbols.comment:
Resolve when ordinary traversal from the conversation, or from every ownerless conversation, reaches no live
non-background task.

symbols.name: TaskScheduler.abortConversation
symbols.signature: async abortConversation(conversationId: ConversationId, background: boolean, context: Context): Promise<void>
symbols.comment:
`Conversation.abort()`: in one commit, withdraw the queued inputs and mark every live non-background task that
ordinary traversal from the conversation reaches; resolves once the scope is idle. With `background`, traversal
crosses background boundaries, and the wait also covers every task it reached.

symbols.name: TaskScheduler.#contextRetentionMs
symbols.comment:
`settings.contextRetentionMs`, or 0 when the host's settings throw. Kept contexts are only a cache, so dropping them
is safe, while a throw here would escape commit listeners, reconciliation, and the expiry timer.

symbols.name: TaskScheduler.#settleIdle
symbols.comment: Resolve idle waiters, and drop each kept context whose conversation has been idle for the retention period.

symbols.name: TaskScheduler.#scheduleExpiry
symbols.comment:
Run `#settleIdle()` when the earliest idle context expires, on a background timer, which never keeps the process
alive. Where the host declines it, as the default does in Cloudflare Workers, none is kept: a pending timer could
keep a Durable Object from being evicted, and eviction frees the contexts. There, task changes alone check expiry.

symbols.name: TaskScheduler.#reconcile
symbols.comment:
One commit that applies what committed records imply: abort marks below live owners with cancellation intent
(spec §5.4), `failFast` marks (spec §5.5), withdrawn queued inputs below cancelled owners, and the final terminal
record of every `completing` task whose ordinary owned work is gone. The durable records are the intent, so this
also repairs whatever a crash left unapplied. Resolves idle waiters that the loaded edges decide.

symbols.name: TaskScheduler.#reconcileWork
symbols.comment: Whether a reconcile pass would have work: a cascade to derive, held outcomes to check, or `failFast` waits.

symbols.name: TaskScheduler.#anyFailed
symbols.comment: Whether any of `ids` holds or ended with an outcome other than `completed`.

symbols.name: TaskScheduler.#finalize
symbols.comment:
Write the terminal record of every `completing` task without live ordinary owned work. Finalizing one can free its
owner, so this repeats over the commit's candidates until nothing changes. A held scheduler outcome gets its
Harness cleanup here.

symbols.name: TaskScheduler.#loadScopes
symbols.comment:
Load the owner chains of the tasks in `#unloaded` and, with `queued`, of every conversation with queued inputs,
on the Session line; returns the latter. Reads committed Storage directly, so it may run inside a commit callback.

symbols.name: TaskScheduler.#loadChain
symbols.comment:
Load the owner edges and task nodes from `start` up to its ownerless root. A known task outside `#unloaded` ends the
walk, as its chain is loaded; the `#unloaded` tasks passed have a loaded chain afterwards. Loading a node can reveal
a cancelled owner, so it makes the next reconcile derive cascade marks.

symbols.name: TaskScheduler.#settle
symbols.comment: Know a terminal task a chain load read, so walks pass through it; its own chain is not loaded yet.

symbols.name: TaskScheduler.#dropIfUnneeded
symbols.comment: Queue an ended task or a conversation for the sweep when nothing is listed below it.

symbols.name: TaskScheduler.#scheduleSweep
symbols.comment:
Sweep in a job of its own on the Session line, after the operation underway: a rejected commit, one with nothing to
write, and a read publish nothing, so the sweep at the end of `#observe` would not run for what they loaded.

symbols.name: TaskScheduler.#sweep
symbols.comment:
Drop the queued nodes that are still unneeded: not live, nothing listed below. Runs once a publication is fully
tracked, and as a job of its own on the line, never inside an operation: work a commit creates below a chain its
own callback loaded keeps that chain. A flat loop: unlisting already queued every node on the way up that lost its
last listed node.

symbols.name: TaskScheduler.#track
symbols.comment:
Bring the scheduler's sets in line with a task's committed record. A task that ended may free the nearest live task
above it: one holding its outcome finalizes, an abort-marked one runs its abort handler; its waiters may run.

symbols.name: TaskScheduler.#release
symbols.comment: The nearest live task above ended ordinary work may be free now: one holding its outcome, or an aborting one.

symbols.name: TaskScheduler.#relist
symbols.comment:
List `start` under its parent node in `#below` while it is a live task or has nodes listed below it, and unlist it
otherwise; then its parent, as far up as that changes. So `#below` holds exactly the tree around live work; a
parent that loses its last listed node is queued for the sweep. A loop, as ownership chains can be deeper than the
call stack.

symbols.name: TaskScheduler.#nearestLiveAbove
symbols.comment:
The nearest live task above ended ordinary work `node`, in the overlay's view: the one that work held, if any. Work
at or below a background task holds nothing above it.

symbols.name: TaskScheduler.#known
symbols.comment: Whether the chain above `node` is loaded, without walking: known tasks outside `#unloaded` have a loaded chain.

symbols.name: TaskScheduler.#edge
symbols.signature: #edge(id: ConversationId, overlay?: Overlay): TaskId | null | undefined
symbols.comment: Owner task of a conversation, `null` when ownerless, `undefined` while not loaded.

symbols.name: TaskScheduler.#above
symbols.comment: Walk up from `start`: owner tasks and conversations, ending at an ownerless root or an edge not loaded yet.

symbols.name: TaskScheduler.#walkDown
symbols.comment:
The tasks below `start` that a walk down reaches: those `#below` lists and, under an overlay, the commit's new tasks,
with its candidates in place of committed records. Background tasks are reached but not entered, unless
`crossBackground`, and neither are the tasks `enter` rejects. A loop, as chains can be deeper than the call stack.

symbols.name: TaskScheduler.#links
symbols.comment:
The links walks down need for the commit's new tasks: each one under its parent node, then each node above it that
`#below` does not list yet, until one it lists, a live task (always listed), or the chain's end.

symbols.name: TaskScheduler.#scheduleWake

symbols.signature:
async #step(
		invocation: Invocation,
		decide: (tx: Transaction, current: ErasedRunningTask) => Decision,
	): Promise<ErasedRunningTask | undefined>
symbols.comment:
One synchronous decision on the Session line. A task that is no longer running (rule 1: terminal, `completing`,
`waiting`, or `sleeping`) or a closing Harness (rule 2) ends the invocation without a write; otherwise `decide` may
stage a write and returns whether the invocation continues. Ending happens inside the callback, before a fault's
Harness cleanup. A rejected step, such as admission after close, also ends the invocation.

symbols.signature: async #terminate(tx: Transaction, record: AnyTaskRecord, outcome: SchedulerOutcome): Promise<void>

its Harness cleanup waits for the final commit (spec §5.5, rule 4); otherwise it is terminal with its cleanup.

symbols.name: TaskScheduler.#commitState
symbols.signature:
async #commitState(
		tx: Transaction,
		invocation: Invocation,
		current: ErasedRunningTask,
		next: NextTaskState<Checkpoint, JsonValue>,
	): Promise<void>
symbols.comment:
Replace a running task's state with what it committed. A terminal state holds as `completing` while ordinary owned
work is live, judged on the commit's candidates, so work the same commit creates below the task counts. A wait is
validated first.

symbols.name: TaskScheduler.#validateWait
symbols.signature:
async #validateWait(
		tx: Transaction,
		invocation: Invocation,
		current: ErasedRunningTask,
		on: readonly TaskId[],
		policy: string,
	): Promise<void>
symbols.comment:
A wait names existing tasks, and `failFast` only tasks the waiter owns. It may not close a cycle in the wait-for
graph, whose edges run from each task to what it waits on and to its live ordinary owned work (spec §5.5); waiting
on itself or on an owner holding it are the shortest such cycles. An abort handler cannot wait.

Invariant: the wait-for graph is acyclic. Only a wait adds an edge between existing tasks, as a new task has only
incoming edges, so checking each wait maintains it.

symbols.name: TaskScheduler.#waitCycle
symbols.signature: async #waitCycle(task: TaskId, on: readonly TaskId[], overlay: Overlay): Promise<TaskId[] | undefined>
symbols.comment:
The path from a member of `on` back to `task` in the wait-for graph, if the wait would close a cycle (spec §5.1).
An edge X -> Y means X cannot settle before Y: Y is in the `on` of waiting X that is not abort-marked, or Y is live
ordinary owned work of X,
which holds X as `completing`. Each task is visited once and each subtree walked once, so a check is bounded by the
live work it reaches.

symbols.name: admitSubmission
symbols.signature:
export async function admitSubmission(
	tx: Tx,
	conversationId: ConversationId,
	draft: SubmissionDraft,
	now: number,
	queueModes: QueueModes,
	span?: TelemetrySpan,
): Promise<Admission>
symbols.comment:
Admit a submission inside a commit (spec §6); `Conversation.submit()` and conversation-owned compactions share it. A
known request ID returns its existing submission without writing. A display-only write (only `kind` and `data`) is
appended and settled `done` at once, busy or not, as it changes nothing the model sees; only behind a queued reset it
queues, so it lands after the reset instead of before it in the context the reset ends. A busy conversation queues anything else in
`pi.inbox`, or rejects `whenBusy: "reject"` input with `ConversationBusy`. An idle conversation with queued items
queues it behind them and runs a final boundary. Otherwise idle input places its entry (`pi.user`, or the input's
own) and starts a run, and an idle write appends its entry and settles `done`, or `stale` when its head reaches
before the active range.

symbols.name: ToolExecutionApi.executeTool
symbols.comment:
Run tool `name` as a nested call of this one and wait for its result. The nested call is its own `pi.tool` task,
owned by this call: it resolves the tool among the conversation's tools, validates, runs the `ToolTask` hooks (which
see `call.parent`), applies output limits and the tool's replay policy, and reports progress in `pi.live.nestedTools`.
Its result returns here instead of entering the transcript. A call that is blocked, invalid, throws, is interrupted,
or is aborted returns an `isError` result.

The nested call's key names it within this call; its call ID is `<callId>/<key>`. By default the key is the call's
position among this invocation's nested calls, `1`, `2`, ... An explicit `key` must be non-empty, without `/`, not
`__proto__`, and not a positive integer, so it never collides with a default one. A rerun of a replay-safe tool
that makes a call with a used key, by calling in the same order or by passing the same `key`, gets that nested call
back, finished or still running, instead of starting another. A nested call a crash interrupted before its result
committed follows its own replay policy, so this is not exactly-once execution. Reusing a key with another tool or
other arguments throws. A tool that is not replay-safe never reruns: after a restart, its unfinished nested calls
are abandoned (`TaskOptions.abandonOnRestart`) before they run again.

`progress: false` commits no running output, details, or diagnostics to the nested call's slot, only its status;
the result still carries its details and diagnostics, and a schema-less tool's output as `structuredOutput`. An
interrupted or aborted call's result is built from its slot, so it then has none of them. Either way, programs never
get the partial output of an interrupted or aborted call.

Nested calls run as soon as they are made, whatever their `executionMode`; the caller decides what runs at once by
what it awaits. Cancelling `context` stops only the wait; the nested call runs on. When this call settles, nested
calls it left running are aborted first. A nested result's `usage` is already counted under its tool; a result
that passes it on counts it again. Rejects, instead of returning a result, once `execute()` has returned, when this
call is aborted, or when the Harness closes.

symbols.name: createPhotonImages
symbols.comment:
An `ImageProcessor` on Photon (Rust compiled to WebAssembly), for `createCodingTools({ images })`. `wasm` is
Photon's `photon_rs_bg.wasm` as bytes or as a compiled module: `@earendil-works/pi-durable/images/node` reads it from
the installed package, `@earendil-works/pi-durable/images/cloudflare` imports it as a Workers module. Elsewhere, such
as a browser, fetch the file and pass its bytes. Photon loads once per process; later calls reuse the first `wasm`.

An image already upright, in a format providers take inline, and within the limits is returned as it is, once it
decodes. Otherwise it is turned upright by its EXIF orientation, scaled to the
maximum width and height, and encoded as PNG or JPEG at falling qualities (JPEG first for JPEG sources), then at
smaller dimensions, 3/4 at a time, until the base64 fits. Formats providers do not take inline (BMP) become PNG.

The work runs on the calling thread: about a second and a half for a 12-megapixel photo. Decoding takes the image's
RGBA size in WebAssembly memory, which does not shrink again; leave the processor out on memory-constrained hosts.

symbols.comment:
`image` at `size` in the first encoding whose base64 fits `maxBytes`: PNG, then JPEG at falling qualities, or the
JPEG qualities first when `jpegFirst`; `undefined` if none fits.

symbols.comment:

symbols.name: SessionImpl
symbols.comment:
Session kernel: one mutation line, the loaded document tracker cache, and committed publication.

The cache is bounded by use: a document with no watch attached leaves it once it was not read or
written for the retention period, and the next access loads it from Storage. Eviction runs as a job on the mutation
line, so no transaction ever holds a tracker that leaves.

Only committed state is observable. Every commit callback, preparation, Storage settlement, adoption, and
publication enqueue runs while the line is held; listeners run later.

Storage failures are final. Every Storage call goes through one guard: the first error a Storage method throws, other
than for a cancelled caller, fails the Session, as does a commit it cannot adopt. That call gets the error; every later
call and every Storage call still underway gets `SessionFailed`; close listeners run at once with the error, and the
Session then closes itself, Storage included, and `closed` settles. Nothing retries: transient errors are the
Storage's to retry. Reopening recovers from what was committed.

symbols.name: ReportInfo
symbols.comment:
What a report to `HarnessOptions.onReport` is about. `extension`, where present, names the extension whose code
failed, when known; for a task's own code, the one that installed the definition the task ran.
- `session_failed`: the error failed the Session, which closes: a Storage error, often a platform reset.
- `task_faulted`: the task ended `faulted`: its phase threw (`reason: "threw"`), or its abort handler was cut off
  `settings.restartLimit` times (`reason: "restart_limit"`).
- `task_parked`: the restart limit parked the task until `Harness.retryTask()`.
- `migration_failed`: the task's stored state could not be migrated; it is blocked until the registry changes.
- `task_outdated`: a running task keeps running under its old definition, which was uninstalled (`missing_task`)
  or replaced by one that cannot take over its state (`incompatible_task`).
- `task_error`: the task's own `runtime.report()`, or a failure in running it.
- `extension_error`: a hook, a section, a wrapper, or a tool's invalid structured output; with the task that ran it,
  or, outside a task, the conversation whose agent was resolved.
- `host_error`: a host callback threw; with the task that called it, if one did.
- `listener_error`: a commit, close, watch, view, or document listener threw.

symbols.name: SetTimer
symbols.comment:
A host timer, given as `HarnessOptions.setTimer`: call `callback` once, about `delayMs` from now, and return
a function that disarms it. `background` timers only free memory, and a host may decline one by returning
`undefined`, for example where a pending timer keeps the process from hibernating; the Harness then frees that memory
at later commits. Other timers pace or resume work: one the host throws on or declines is armed with `setTimeout`.
A timer should not fire early; callers check their clock again when it fires.

symbols.name: Storage
symbols.comment:
Atomic persistence boundary for Session records.

Storage trusts the owning Session to supply semantically valid records, references,
ancestry, and transitions. Implementations enforce atomicity, global ID ownership,
immutable conversation/entry creation, document record consistency, and detached values;
Session serializes commits.

An error a method throws is final: it fails the Session, which nothing retries, so retry transient failures inside
the method. Two errors of a read fail only that read: a `StorageRequestError` for an invalid request (an unknown
conversation, a foreign or malformed cursor, history a document does not keep), which must have no durable effect, and a
rejection because its caller's context was aborted. Any error from `commit()` or `mintId()` is fatal.

symbols.name: Storage.commit
symbols.signature: commit(writes: readonly StorageWrite[], adopt: (seq: Seq) => void, context: Context): Promise<Seq>;
symbols.comment:
Atomically persist one batch and return its sequence. Once the batch is durable, call `adopt(seq)` exactly once,
synchronously and before this storage's next commit starts, then resolve with `seq`; a commit that fails before it
is durable never calls `adopt`. `adopt` is the caller's in-memory adoption of the batch, so memory always shows a
complete prefix of the log; it must not throw. Once resolved, later reads through this storage observe the batch.

Entries are immutable. `model` holds the messages an entry contributes to

the next model request; `data` is for the app only. context() turns the

stored transcript into those request messages:

- an entry with `head` starts a new context; older entries stay stored,

- `edits` replace or omit what an earlier entry contributes,

- aborted, error, and deferred assistant messages are not sent,

- tool results are sent right after their call, in call order,

- a call without a result gets a synthesized error result.

symbols.name: payments
symbols.comment:
A task is a small state machine. Its state, the checkpoint, is saved after

every step, so after a crash the next open continues from the last saved

the result. A crash between doing and saving reruns that step, so the step

must be safe to repeat; here the fake payment service ignores a repeated key.

symbols.name: Subagent
symbols.comment:
─── Product code ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Each subagent is its own conversation with its own transcript, so it remembers earlier messages. The main

conversation keeps a small document that maps subagent names to their conversations. Documents are durable state

next to a transcript, changed in commits like entries.

symbols.name: reported
symbols.comment: Answers already reported to the main agent: several messages can end in one answer, reported once.

symbols.name: Anchor
symbols.comment:
Every task and conversation has an owner, and that decides what an abort or an idle wait reaches: aborting a task

aborts what it owns, and waiting for a conversation to be idle waits for its work. A subagent must outlive the main

agent's turns, so its conversation is owned by an anchor: a background task that finishes at once. A background task

is a boundary: the main agent's Esc and idle waits stop there, but `abort({ background: true })` still reaches past

it, so a host can stop everything.

symbols.name: ReporterInput
symbols.signature: type ReporterInput = { name: string; conversationId: ConversationId; message: string; followUp: boolean };
symbols.comment:
A reporter delivers one message to a subagent and reports the answer to the main agent. It is a background task

too, so the main agent's Esc and idle waits leave it alone. Tasks are durable: each phase ends with a saved

checkpoint, and after a restart the task continues from the last one. Request IDs make a repeated submission return

the first one, so the subagent gets the message once and the main agent gets the report once.
symbols.output: { name: string; conversationId: ConversationId; message: string; followUp: boolean }

symbols.name: Editor.computeVerticalMoveColumn
symbols.comment:
Compute the target visual column for vertical cursor movement.
Implements the sticky column decision table:

| P | S | T | U | Scenario                                             | Set Preferred | Move To     |
|---|---|---|---| ---------------------------------------------------- |---------------|-------------|
| 0 | * | 0 | - | Start nav, target fits                               | null          | current     |
| 0 | * | 1 | - | Start nav, target shorter                            | current       | target end  |
| 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | Clamped, target fits preferred                       | null          | preferred   |
| 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | Clamped, target longer but still can't fit preferred | keep          | target end  |
| 1 | 0 | 1 | - | Clamped, target even shorter                         | keep          | target end  |
| 1 | 1 | 0 | - | Rewrapped, target fits current                       | null          | current     |
| 1 | 1 | 1 | - | Rewrapped, target shorter than current               | current       | target end  |

Where:
- P = preferred col is set
- S = cursor in middle of source line (not clamped to end)
- T = target line shorter than current visual col
- U = target line shorter than preferred col

symbols.comment:
Keyboard input handling for terminal applications.

Supports both legacy terminal sequences and Kitty keyboard protocol.
See: https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/keyboard-protocol/
Reference: https://github.com/sst/opentui/blob/7da92b4088aebfe27b9f691c04163a48821e49fd/packages/core/src/lib/parse.keypress.ts

Symbol keys are also supported, however some ctrl+symbol combos
overlap with ASCII codes, e.g. ctrl+[ = ESC.
See: https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/keyboard-protocol/#legacy-ctrl-mapping-of-ascii-keys
Those can still be * used for ctrl+shift combos

API:
- matchesKey(data, keyId) - Check if input matches a key identifier
- parseKey(data) - Parse input and return the key identifier
- Key - Helper object for creating typed key identifiers
- setKittyProtocolActive(active) - Set global Kitty protocol state
- isKittyProtocolActive() - Query global Kitty protocol state

Keyboard input handling for terminal applications.

Supports both legacy terminal sequences and Kitty keyboard protocol.
See: https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/keyboard-protocol/

packages/tui/src/stdin-buffer.ts.comment:
StdinBuffer buffers input and emits complete sequences.

This is necessary because stdin data events can arrive in partial chunks,
especially for escape sequences like mouse events. Without buffering,
partial sequences can be misinterpreted as regular keypresses.

For example, the mouse SGR sequence `\x1b[<35;20;5m` might arrive as:
- Event 1: `\x1b`
- Event 2: `[<35`
- Event 3: `;20;5m`

The buffer accumulates these until a complete sequence is detected.
Call the `process()` method to feed input data.

Based on code from OpenTUI (https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui)
MIT License - Copyright (c) 2025 opentui

Set up StdinBuffer to split batched input into individual sequences.
This ensures components receive single events, making matchesKey/isKeyRelease work correctly.

Also watches for Kitty protocol response and enables it when detected.
This is done here (after stdinBuffer parsing) rather than on raw stdin

symbols.name: ProcessTerminal.queryAndEnableKittyProtocol
symbols.comment:
Query terminal for Kitty keyboard protocol support and enable it if available.

Kitty's progressive enhancement detection requires requesting the desired
flags before querying them. The trailing DA query is a sentinel supported by
terminals that do not know Kitty keyboard protocol; receiving DA before a
Kitty response enables modifyOtherKeys fallback without a startup timeout.

The requested flags are:
- 1 = disambiguate escape codes
- 2 = report event types (press/repeat/release)
- 4 = report alternate keys (shifted key, base layout key)

The OSC 7501 program status query shares the DA sentinel: a terminal that supports it replies
before DA. `PI_PROGRAM_STATUS=1` or `0` skips the query.

symbols.name: BoundedTerminalWriter
symbols.comment:
Streams terminal output in 1 MiB chunks so a full render never forms one string large enough to exceed V8's limit.

`append()` fills the current chunk and flushes it when full. Oversized input is split at chunk boundaries, preserving
surrogate pairs so each write remains valid UTF-16. Callers append synchronized-output begin/end sequences themselves;
the final `flush()` writes any remainder, including the end sequence.

symbols.name: BoundedTerminalWriter.append

Append terminal data, flushing full chunks as needed. Callers must call `flush()` after the final append.
@param value Terminal data to write in order; oversized values are split without splitting surrogate pairs.

scripts/check-entry-graphs.mjs.comment:
Entry points are cost contracts.

A package's `exports` map is the only place that says which modules are public, and one stray
`export *` can silently make a narrow entry drag an entire barrel: importing a 1-file pure
function through a barrel costs ~37 MB of evaluated module graph, and nothing fails until someone
measures a process. This walks the value-import graph of every declared entry point and enforces a
budget per entry, so that regression fails at commit time instead.

Only value imports count. `import type` / `export type` are erased before Node sees them.

scripts/check-model-catalog-compat.mjs.comment:
Checks that released pi versions can use the model catalog we are about to publish.



Problem: pi.dev serves each published catalog to every released pi at or above

MINIMUM_PI_VERSION. Released clients use it right away, without updating pi.

If the catalog needs code they don't have, they break.



Example: a catalog moved the kimi-coding models from anthropic-messages to

openai-completions. pi 1.2.0's kimi-coding provider only implements

anthropic-messages, so 1.2.0 sent requests to the wrong API and they failed.



Check: build the model list a released client would end up with (its built-in

models, overlaid by the new catalog), and compile the release's pi-ai source

against it. pi-ai's types tie each provider to the APIs it implements, so a

model with an API its provider lacks is a type error.



Only the latest release on npm is checked. If it is older than

MINIMUM_PI_VERSION, no released pi receives the catalog, and the check is skipped.



Usage: node scripts/check-model-catalog-compat.mjs [--catalog <file>]

--catalog <file>  catalog to check (default: .artifacts/model-catalog/models.all.json,

written by `npm run generate:model-catalog`)

scripts/release.mjs.comment:
Release script for pi-mono

Usage:
  node scripts/release.mjs <major|minor|patch>
  node scripts/release.mjs <x.y.z>

Steps:
1. Check for uncommitted changes
2. Verify every public workspace package is registered on npm,
   pin the newest model catalog for Nix, and build with it
3. Bump version via npm run version:xxx or set an explicit version
4. Update CHANGELOG.md files: [Unreleased] -> [version] - date
5. Regenerate release artifacts
6. Run checks and tests
7. Commit and tag the release
8. Add new [Unreleased] section to changelogs
9. Commit next-cycle changelog updates
10. Push main and the tag to trigger CI publication and verified pi.dev announcement

symbols.name: MODEL_TYPES
symbols.comment: Request the typed catalog; its bytes are what a revision hashes.

symbols.name: fetchLiveCatalog
symbols.comment:
Discover the newest published catalog. It is generated from main, which is
what this checkout builds. Do not send `pi-version`: on main it is the last
released version, and pi.dev answers it with the catalog for released
clients, which predates any `MINIMUM_PI_VERSION` bump main depends on.

symbols.name: modelApiGroups
symbols.comment:
Return the `provider/type/api` model groups the catalog provides for this
checkout's providers. The generated `*.models.ts` types are derived from the
data, which is grouped by API, so code only type-checks when the catalog has
the same groups as main: e.g. OPENCODE_CLASSIFIER_MODELS needs opencode
classifier models, and a provider factory returning
`Provider<"openai-completions">` fails when its models use another API.

symbols.name: hydrateModelCatalogBytes
symbols.comment: Hydrate the checkout's model data from catalog bytes, as the Nix build does.

symbols.name: hydrationProblem
symbols.comment: Return why the catalog cannot hydrate this checkout, or undefined if it can.

symbols.name: updateModelCatalogPin
symbols.signature: export async function updateModelCatalogPin(root, { ifStale = false } = {})
symbols.comment:
Pin the live model catalog for Nix builds. With `ifStale`, keep the current
pin while it still hydrates this checkout and has the same model groups as
the live catalog for the checkout's providers. Returns the pinned revision
and its catalog bytes.

boundaries.title: 普通 CLI 的计划模式和子智能体
boundaries.text: 根 README 明确说明未作为默认功能提供，仓库附带可加载扩展示例。
boundaries.impact: 列入“其他”的示例；Durable 的相应原语单独标为实验。

boundaries.title: 内置权限系统
boundaries.text: Pi 以启动用户和进程的权限运行，不内置完整的文件／进程／网络／凭据访问审批系统。
boundaries.impact: 工具 allowlist、项目 trust、审批扩展示例不能等同于系统沙箱。

boundaries.title: 项目信任保护范围
boundaries.text: 主要控制项目配置和资源加载；sessionDir 在信任前读取，AGENTS 等上下文文件也不以信任为前提。
boundaries.impact: 不能把“拒绝信任”理解为“目录内内容完全不会影响模型”。

boundaries.title: 技能 allowed-tools 字段
boundaries.text: 文档列为实验性元数据；Pi 不因此获得一套通用安全隔离机制。
boundaries.impact: 技能是指导与资源包，不是强制权限执行环境。

boundaries.title: 默认工具集合
boundaries.text: 普通 CLI 默认 read、bash、edit、write；其他内置工具按设置启用。MCP 可激活 codemode／tool_search。
boundaries.impact: “仓库内置”与“当前会话默认可调用”分别标注。

boundaries.title: SDK 内置扩展
boundaries.text: SDK 不自动加载 CLI 的 MCP、Codemode、tool_search，需显式加入工厂并完成绑定。
boundaries.impact: CLI 可用并不代表最小 SDK 示例自动具备全部能力。

boundaries.title: MCP 完整度
boundaries.text: 当前集成支持工具与资源，但不渲染 MCP Apps；独立 MCP README 将 sampling、tasks、旧 SSE 等排除在初始核心之外。
boundaries.impact: 不把“支持 MCP”写成“支持 MCP 的全部规范和应用 UI”。

boundaries.title: 图像生成保存行为
boundaries.text: 模型接口返回图像内容；Codemode 的 `image()` 会另存临时文件。models.md 中“生成图不落盘”与 codemode.md 的表述层级不同且容易混淆。
boundaries.impact: 清单将生成接口和 image 输出／临时保存分开，不承诺永久资产库。

boundaries.title: 模型硬输入限制
boundaries.text: 目录可以声明 request bytes 或每请求图片数，但文档明确 Pi 尚不据此重写或拒绝全部历史。
boundaries.impact: 图片缩放支持不等于所有元数据限制均被运行时强制执行。

boundaries.title: 分类和图像模型
boundaries.text: 不出现在普通聊天 `/model` 选择器，须通过 Codemode／扩展／库的专用接口使用。
boundaries.impact: 不把这些模型列成可直接替代聊天 Agent 的模型。

boundaries.title: 自动重试
boundaries.text: 模型暂时错误、MCP 重连和 Chord 断链是不同机制，Chord 在途请求断链后无法保证是否已执行。
boundaries.impact: 不承诺工具副作用自动重放，重试需由业务决定。

boundaries.title: 普通会话分叉
boundaries.text: 分叉保存对话分支，不自动恢复 Git 工作目录。
boundaries.impact: 代码恢复另见 git-checkpoint 示例。

boundaries.title: Durable 存储锁
boundaries.text: Durable 仍要求单进程拥有存储；新 Chord node 提供独立 processLock，须宿主显式集成。
boundaries.impact: 旧 experimental 宿主已删除，不能把其目录锁视为当前 CLI 能力。

boundaries.title: 外部生态
boundaries.text: Slack／聊天自动化指向独立 pi-chat 仓库；会话发布到 Hugging Face 使用外部工具。
boundaries.impact: 不作为本仓库内置业务模块。

boundaries.title: 其他代理常见功能
boundaries.text: 普通内置工具清单未提供通用浏览器自动化、专用网页搜索、语音转写、邮件客户端或定时任务调度模块。
boundaries.impact: 可借 Shell、MCP、技能或扩展实现，但不能将可扩展性写成现成功能。

boundaries.title: Chord 热重载边界
boundaries.text: 当前仅协调直接子宿主，commit 决策未持久化，重连不能续接旧 holds；loader 不回收旧模块且不隔离插件。
boundaries.impact: 跨进程能力已实现，但不承诺崩溃下原子集群升级、无限层级重载或沙箱。

boundaries.title: Chord 数据所有权
boundaries.text: track、replicatedState 和 replace 接管可信不可变 JSON，发布值并未冻结。
boundaries.impact: 消费者不得修改共享对象，跨可变信任边界须复制或序列化。

boundaries.title: PTY 平台范围
boundaries.text: Env 的远程文件／exec 与交互 PTY 有各自平台范围；历史工作台另有 Windows x64 ConPTY 实现，当前 checkout 不包含。
boundaries.impact: 不把工作台终端支持外推为 Env Windows PTY 支持；需宿主显式启用并校验原生资源。

boundaries.title: 历史工作台身份与 CLI 权限
boundaries.text: 旧 HTTP 宿主实现逐请求身份、工作区授权和来源校验，默认回环监听；原生 CLI 没有相同的 HTTP 身份入口。
boundaries.impact: 进程 worker、路径校验和工具上限不等于 OS 沙箱。

boundaries.title: 历史工作台草稿与真实执行
boundaries.text: 旧浏览器字段、fixture、保存回执、真实模型/daemon/Docker 操作是不同状态。
boundaries.impact: 按 capabilities 与运行证据判断，不以表单存在推断完整运行支持。

boundaries.title: 历史工作台两套设置
boundaries.text: 旧 /api/config 管理模块配置及 revisionVector；/api/settings 桥接原生白名单设置。
boundaries.impact: 两套 null、覆盖和信任规则不同，不互换；原生设置保存影响之后的 runtime 创建。

boundaries.title: 版本与持久化迁移
boundaries.text: Durable 1.4.0 引入的 SQLite schema v2 不能被 1.3.0 或更早版本打开；JSONL 旧版不能恢复 sleeping 任务。
boundaries.impact: 升级需对照当前源码和备份，还需检查 1.4.0 之后的 Unreleased Storage.commit / Watch 契约。
